::: {#def-deviance}

#### Deviance

The **deviance** of a fitted logistic regression is twice the amount by which its maximized log-likelihood falls short of the largest log-likelihood any model could reach on the same labels.
For labels $\outvar_i \in \set{0, 1}$ the largest log-likelihood is $0$,
reached by a model that gives each label probability $1$,
so the deviance is

$$
D \eqdef -2 \, \llikf{\hvcoef}
= -2 \sumin \cb{\outvar_i \ln \hat\prob_i + \paren{1 - \outvar_i} \ln\paren{1 - \hat\prob_i}},
$$ {#eq-deviance}

where $\hat\prob_i = \sigmoidf{\dprod{\hvcoef}{\vpredvar_i}}$ is the fitted probability.

:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" collapse=true}
## Source

@nelder1972generalized introduced the deviance for the whole family of generalized linear models;
logistic regression is the case of Bernoulli outcomes with the logit link.
@hastie2009elements, Section 4.4.3, discusses it for logistic regression.
:::
